title: Finite-presentation modules on a ringed space have a set of isomorphism representatives
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal O_X$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Say that $\mathcal G\in\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ is of finite presentation if every $x\in X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ admitting an exact sequence $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U\to0$ with $m,n$ finite. Then there are a set $I$ and finite-presentation modules $(\mathcal G_i)_{i\in I}$ such that every finite-presentation $\mathcal O_X$-module is isomorphic to some $\mathcal G_i$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BC (lemma-set-isomorphism-classes-finite-type-modules), lines 957-984; apply it because a module of finite presentation is of finite type by Modules, Definition 01BN
